summary: Routing snapback from pin timestamp skew during canary shadow (traffic mirror)
description:
Issue summary:
During a canary shadow (traffic mirroring) attempt for customer LexicoSearch in eu-west, tenant-bound requests briefly reverted from the pinned canary variant back to the primary variant. The tenant explicitly had a model pin set to canary for several days. The behaviour surfaced as ~10-30s windows where streaming responses came from the legacy model (different tokenizer leading to minor token differences) and request latencies spiked.

Impact:
- Customer: LexicoSearch (dedicated) observed degraded output quality for a subset of user sessions and a small billing spike due to fallback to larger primary variant.
- Scope: Intermittent, appears tied to long-lived streaming sessions and canary shadowing config in eu-west. Estimated <0.5% of total requests for the tenant during the window.

Environment:
- Prod, eu-west cluster, control-plane v3.24.1, edge-proxy v2.9.0, orchestrator v1.18.
- Canary config: mirror=true, weight=0 (shadow only), tenant pin -> model: redwood-v2-medium-canary-2026-03-08

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Start a long-lived streaming session pinned to canary via the tenant pin API.
2) Enable canary shadow mirror (mirror=true) for route.
3) Under light-to-moderate traffic, observe streaming output for the session.
4) After a reconciliation window, some streaming chunks show tokens produced by primary variant.

Observed logs (edge/orchestrator snippets):
- edge-proxy[2026-03-10T14:22:11Z] DEBUG route-resolver: tenant=lexico-001 pin-ts=2026-03-08T12:05:33Z source=orchestrator snapshot-id=8421
- orchestrator[2026-03-10T14:22:11Z] INFO reconcile: tenant=lexico-001 last-pin-updated=2026-03-10T14:18:55Z applied-snapshot=8423
- edge-proxy[2026-03-10T14:22:12Z] WARN routing: pin-timestamp-skew detected (edge older than control-plane) -> snapback to primary variant
- serving-runtime[2026-03-10T14:22:12Z] ERROR model-resolve: route=lexico-001 variant=primary returned tokens mismatch md5_expected=7f4a... md5_actual=7f4b...

Notes: The key symptom is a timestamp skew between the edge-side cached pin metadata and the control-plane's most-recent pin. Because shadow mirror snapshots are reconciled on a short window, an older edge cache led the reconciler to interpret the tenant as ‘not pinned’ and therefore apply normal primary routing temporarily (snapback).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 15:00 UTC - Reproduced on staging by mimicking long-lived stream with mirror=true; confirmed edge cache TTL=120s and control-plane pin update time within that TTL.
Hypothesis: edge clock drift / async pin propagation + mirror reconciliation logic treats stale edge pin metadata as absence of pin and triggers snapback path.
Found evidence: edge log shows 'pin-ts' older than orchestrator last-pin-updated in ~12 occurrences across the eu-west pool during the window.
Checked prior related fixes: PRs that modified snapshot reconciliation in 2025 Q4 — behaviour differs when mirror=true vs weight>0.
Temporary mitigation: forced pin-refresh API call for the tenant caused immediate rebind to canary; restarting edge-proxy drained the stale cache and prevented further snapbacks.
Telemetry: added metric 'pin_ts_skew_count' to detect future events and alert threshold set to 5 in 5m for eu-west.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reported streaming tokens diverging after enabling canary shadow. Created ticket and requested SRE look into edge/cache behaviour.
Marco Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-10: Confirmed timestamp skew in logs. Re-produced in staging with long stream. Proposed immediate mitigation: pin refresh + edge-proxy rolling restart in eu-west.
LexicoSearch (Customer) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged workaround is acceptable short term but asked for root cause and a permanent fix timeline.
Emily Zhao (Eng - Orchestrator) 2026-03-11: Noted that reconciler assumes authoritative source = control-plane; edge should not cause snapback if mirror=true. Opening follow-up PR to normalize logic.
Marco Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-12: Rolled edge-proxy restart across eu-west (canary group -> full). Post-restart telemetry shows no further skews for 48h.
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-13: Customer confirmed no further incidents during business hours, requested a summary and PR link for audit.
resolution: Workaround applied: forced tenant pin refresh via control-plane API and rolling restart of edge-proxy fleet in eu-west. Customer-facing mitigation communicated. Permanent fix: engineering patched the reconciliation logic to ignore edge-side absent pin when mirror=true and to accept control-plane pin as authoritative even when edge cache TTL not expired; PRs referenced above. Monitoring: new metric (pin_ts_skew_count) and dashboard added; alerting configured for eu-west. Post-deploy verification: 72h silent period with no recurrence; customer confirmed restoration of expected behaviour. Follow-up action: backport fix to 3.23.x maintenance branch and schedule a postmortem note in Confluence.
